items.question: How are the planetary and stellar distances measured upward from the earth?
premises: From earth up to Saturn there is a group of five planets.
Each interval in that group is known by tradition.
From the sun the group of seven sages is one lakh away, and from that the pole star is likewise placed.
items.inference: The cosmic levels above earth are arranged in fixed measured intervals from planet to planet and then to the stellar realms.
uncertainties: The exact unit implied by each interval in the first group is not stated explicitly in this verse.
items.plain_english: From the earth up to Saturn, the wise know a set of five planets, each at its own interval. From the sun, the realm of the Seven Sages is one lakh away, and from there the Pole Star is placed at the same distance.

items.question: What is the nature and position of the pole star in the cosmic order?
premises: The unmoving pole star is Brahma himself in a lower form.
It stands in the place of Brahma as the central pivot of celestial cars.
It is located above all of them.
items.inference: The pole star functions as the fixed Brahmic axis that supports and crowns the revolving celestial realms.
items.plain_english: The unmoving Pole Star is Brahma himself in a lower form, stationed in Brahma's place. It has become the central pivot of all celestial cars and stands above them all.

items.question: What holds all the realms together in the region of the pole star?
premises: In that region all things are understood to be bound within the sphere of wind.
There are seven heavenly masses of wind.
These masses chiefly begin with the cloud-bearing winds and extend upward.
items.inference: The cosmic realms around the pole star are structurally supported by a graded system of seven wind masses.
uncertainties: The precise identity of each of the seven wind masses is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: Here, all things are understood to be bound within the sphere of wind. There are seven heavenly wind masses, chiefly beginning with the clouds and the like.

items.question: What happens to ritual performers who lack liberating knowledge?
premises: Those who perform sacrifices and offerings but lack knowledge go to heaven.
When the fruit of that heaven is exhausted, they do not remain there.
By the remainder of their merit they return to the human world.
items.inference: Ritual merit without knowledge grants only a temporary ascent to heaven followed by return to human birth.
items.plain_english: Those who perform sacrifices and other rites but lack knowledge go to heaven. When that merit is exhausted, they return to the human world because of the merit that still remains.

items.question: What are the measured distances from earth to the pole star and from heaven to the great world?
premises: The span from earth up to the pole star is fifteen lakhs.
The span from heaven to the great world is two crores and eighty-five lakhs.
These figures summarize the vertical scale of the lower cosmic regions.
items.inference: The text gives precise numerical measures to map the vast distances between the major cosmic levels.
uncertainties: The unit of distance is not named in this verse, though lakhs and crores are standard yojana measures in this context.
items.plain_english: Thus, from the earth up to the Pole Star the distance is fifteen lakhs. From heaven up to the Great World it is two crores and eighty-five lakhs.

items.question: Who dwells in the great world above heaven?
premises: Seers, sages, and perfected beings such as Markandeya are established there.
Gods whose cosmic duties have been completed also abide there.
This world is the Great World reached above heaven.
items.inference: The Great World is a realm for advanced beings and for gods who have finished their appointed offices.
items.plain_english: In the Great World dwell seers, sages, and perfected beings such as Markandeya. Gods whose duties have come to an end also abide there.

items.question: What lies between the great world and the jana world, and who lives there?
premises: In the great intermediate space there are other beings who still enjoy cosmic office.
The jana world is eight crores above the great world.
In the jana world dwell Kapila and others.
items.inference: Above the Great World the cosmos includes an intermediate office-bearing realm and then the jana world inhabited by sages like Kapila.
items.plain_english: In the great intermediate space there are others who still hold office. Eight crores above the Great World is the Jana world, where Kapila and others dwell.

items.question: Who inhabits the jana and tapas worlds in this cosmic ascent?
premises: In the jana world many happy Sadhyas also dwell.
The tapas world is one crore above the jana world.
In the tapas world dwell Sanaka and others of great wisdom.
items.inference: The ascent continues through realms of blessed beings and then to a higher world of great sages.
items.plain_english: Many happy Sadhyas dwell there as well. One crore above the Jana world is the Tapas world, where Sanaka and others of great wisdom reside.

items.question: What office is exercised in the tapas world and what lies above it?
premises: In the tapas world the lords of creatures born from Brahma exercise their office.
Above the tapas world lies the abode of Brahma, called Satya.
The Satya world is sixteen crores above the tapas world.
items.inference: The tapas world is an administrative realm of Brahma-born progenitors, leading upward to Brahma's own Satya world.
items.plain_english: There the lords of creatures born from Brahma hold their office. Above the Tapas world, sixteen crores away, is Satya, the abode of Brahma.

items.question: What takes place in the Satya world under the self-born Brahma?
premises: The self-born Brahma dwells in the Satya world and manifests this universe.
The Vedas are present in that world.
Others refined by action and meditation also dwell there.
items.inference: Satya is the world of Brahma's cosmic manifestation and of beings perfected through Vedic action and meditation.
items.plain_english: There the self-born Brahma dwells and manifests this universe. In the Satya world are the Vedas and others who have been refined by action and meditation.

items.question: What realms lie above the Satya world in the ascent toward Vishnu?
premises: Above Satya, one crore higher, are beings fixed in bliss at the seat of Brahma.
Two crores above Brahma's seat is the city of Vishnu.
These levels continue the measured vertical order of the cosmos.
items.inference: Beyond Satya the path rises through Brahma's seat to the still higher realm of Vishnu.
items.plain_english: There, above, one crore higher, are those established in bliss at Brahma's seat. Two crores above Brahma's seat is the city of Vishnu.

items.question: How do devotees reach Vishnu's abode and what lies beyond it?
premises: Devotees of Vishnu reach his abode through meditation, worship, and recitation.
Seven crores above the world of Vishnu is the world of the supreme lord.
The ascent continues by measured stages beyond Vishnu.
items.inference: Vishnu's realm is attained by devotion, but it is not the final summit in this cosmic hierarchy.
uncertainties: The verse names the next realm as that of the supreme lord; the following verse clarifies it as Rudra's.
items.plain_english: Devotees of Vishnu reach that abode through meditation, worship, and recitation. Seven crores above Vishnu's world is the world of the supreme lord.

items.question: Which worshippers are associated with Rudra's realm within the cosmic egg?
premises: Rudra is the maker of creation and dissolution within the path of the cosmic egg.
Some worshippers are devoted to the linga.
Those worshippers lack initiation and liberating knowledge.
items.inference: External linga worship without initiation and knowledge connects a person to Rudra's cosmic domain but not to final release.
items.plain_english: Rudra is the maker of creation and dissolution within the cosmic egg. Those who are devoted to worship of the linga but lack initiation and knowledge are connected with his realm.

items.question: What is the destiny of those who reach Rudra's city within the cosmic egg?
premises: Such worshippers go to Rudra's city within the cosmic egg and never fall downward.
All who stand there eventually go to Shiva.
They become Rudras initiated by Srikantha.
items.inference: Rudra's city is a stable intermediate realm from which initiated beings ultimately ascend to Shiva.
items.plain_english: They go to Rudra's city within the cosmic egg and never fall back down. All who dwell there eventually go to Shiva, becoming Rudras initiated by Srikantha.

items.question: How do the Rudras ascend after their office in Rudra's city ends?
premises: When their office is exhausted, they do not remain in the same place.
They ascend together with the group of Rudra's daughters.
They move from city to city above Rudra in ever higher stages.
items.inference: The Rudra realm is part of a graduated ascent in which office-bearing beings rise through successive higher cities.
items.plain_english: When their office comes to an end, they ascend together with the group of Rudra's daughters, going from city to city above Rudra in ever higher stages.

items.question: What role does the staff-bearing guardian play in relation to the cosmic egg and liberation?
premises: Below the cosmic egg and above Rudra is the city of the staff-bearer.
By Shiva's will he makes the cosmic egg firm.
He also makes the path of liberation possible.
items.inference: The staff-bearer is both a cosmic stabilizer of the egg and a guardian who enables passage on the path to liberation.
items.plain_english: Below the cosmic egg and above Rudra is the city of the staff-bearer. By Shiva's will he holds the egg firm and also opens the path of liberation.

items.question: Who are the seven world-lords ruling upward from the earth world?
premises: The verse lists Sharva, Rudra, Bhima, Bhava, Ugra, the great lord, and Ishana.
These seven are lords of worlds beginning from the earth world.
They are described as Shiva-forms.
items.inference: The cosmic hierarchy from the earth world upward is governed by seven successive Shiva-lords.
uncertainties: The phrase rendered as 'great then' may refer to Mahadeva as a distinct lord in the sequence.
items.plain_english: Sharva, Rudra, Bhima, Bhava, Ugra, the great lord, and Ishana are the seven Shiva-lords of the worlds, ruling upward from the earth world.

items.question: How are the lower and higher worlds distinguished in their composition?
premises: Seven worlds are begun by gross particulars.
The higher worlds are begun by subtle particulars.
The teacher explained this properly in the Ruru scripture.
items.inference: The cosmic worlds are structured in two tiers, with gross elements forming the lower seven and subtle elements forming those beyond.
items.plain_english: Seven worlds are formed from gross particulars, while the higher worlds are formed from subtle ones. The teacher explained this clearly in the Ruru scripture.

items.question: What are the gross particulars from which the seven lower worlds arise?
premises: In Brahma's first creation, five gross particulars called abundant were made from his own body.
A seventh element is made of them.
The seven worlds are composed from these.
items.inference: The lower seven worlds arise from five gross elemental particulars produced in Brahma's primal creation, together with their composite form.
uncertainties: The identity of the seventh 'made-of-them' element is not named explicitly in this verse.
items.plain_english: In Brahma's first creation, five gross particulars called the abundant ones were made from his own body. With a seventh formed from them, these became the basis of the seven worlds.

items.question: What supports the worlds beyond the gross lower realms?
premises: Beyond the lower worlds there are subtle supports.
These supports are subtle great elements born from the tanmatras and associated with subtle bodies.
They uphold the coverings of the worlds mutually through qualities such as smell and the rest.
items.inference: The higher worlds are structured by subtle tanmatric elements that serve as mutually supporting coverings.
items.plain_english: Beyond that, the worlds are supported by subtle coverings: great elements born from the tanmatras, upheld through subtle bodies and mutually connected by smell and the other subtle qualities.

items.question: What is the measured extent from the fire of time to the staff-bearer and what bounds the egg above?
premises: From the fire of time up to the staff-bearer the distance is eighty-eight crores.
Above that, within the cosmic egg, there is a shell.
That shell is solid and one crore yojanas thick.
items.inference: The cosmic egg has a vast measured interior culminating below a dense outer shell of enormous thickness.
items.plain_english: From the fire of time up to the staff-bearer the distance is eighty-eight crores. Above that, within the cosmic egg, is a solid shell one crore yojanas thick.

items.question: What is the total vertical extent of the earth sphere and how is it pictured?
premises: There are fifty crores above the surface of the earth and likewise fifty crores below.
Together this makes one hundred crores for the earth sphere.
From that measure it is pictured like a golden grain of rice.
items.inference: The earth sphere is conceived as a vast but bounded whole, symmetrically extended and imagistically compared to a golden rice grain.
items.plain_english: There are fifty crores above the earth's surface and fifty crores below, making the earth sphere one hundred crores in all. From that it is pictured like a golden grain of rice.

items.question: What force breaks the hard cosmic boundary and how are the hundred Rudras arranged outside it?
premises: The mantra reaching up to the hundred Rudras, with hum and phat, splits that hard-to-pacify boundary.
Ten Rudras are placed in each direction.
Thus there are one hundred Rudras outside.
items.inference: The cosmic boundary is overcome by Rudra-mantra power, and the hundred Rudras are stationed directionally as its outer guardians.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic role of 'hum phat' in the verse is compressed; it is taken as the mantra syllables effecting the splitting.
items.plain_english: The mantra extending to the hundred Rudras, with the syllables hum and phat, splits that hard-to-pacify boundary. Ten by ten in every direction, there are a hundred Rudras outside.

items.question: How is the cosmic egg supported and described by authoritative teachers?
premises: That structure supports the cosmic egg.
It does so by its own power on all sides.
The teachers in the Raurava and other scriptures describe it as having the form of an egg.
items.inference: The cosmic egg is a self-supported, all-encompassing egg-shaped structure affirmed by scriptural authorities.
items.plain_english: That which supports the cosmic egg does so by its own power on all sides. The teachers, in the Raurava and other scriptures, have said that it has the form of an egg.
